business: duckbro (duckbro.store, humorous duck-themed socks, bags and accessories, pre-launch)
target: Adults 18 to 38 in the EU and UK who shop online for humorous, meme-style fashion for themselves or as a gift
where: EU and UK, online (Instagram, TikTok, the brand's own website)

behaviours.name: Gift hunter
behaviours.how: Buys fun, low-risk presents for birthdays, Secret Santa and colleagues; cares about arriving on time.

behaviours.name: Meme-humour fan
behaviours.how: Buys things that are a joke you can wear; shares them online.

behaviours.name: TikTok/Instagram impulse buyer
behaviours.how: Buys from ads and creators in the moment if checkout is easy.

behaviours.name: Fun-socks collector
behaviours.how: Already owns many patterned socks from Happy Socks, Stance or similar and compares designs and quality.

behaviours.name: Sustainability-minded
behaviours.how: Prefers made-to-order, recycled materials, small brands; distrusts greenwashing.

behaviours.name: Bargain and discount-code hunter
behaviours.how: Waits for codes, compares with Amazon, Primark or AliExpress versions.

behaviours.name: Review-checker
behaviours.how: Won't buy from a brand with no reviews, Trustpilot page or proof it ships.

objections: Pre-order? I want it now, not 'once 100 people reserve'
I've never heard of this brand, will it actually ship?
€30 for socks is a lot when Primark has funny socks for €5
Is the duck joke funny for more than a week?
Why pay €4.99 just to reserve something?
There are no real reviews on the product pages
Is it really better quality than the cheap knock-offs?
habits: you have a colleague's birthday coming up
you do Secret Santa with friends every December
you already own a drawer of patterned socks
you shop on Zalando and ASOS for most clothes
you follow a few small streetwear brands on Instagram
